subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should this issue be narrowed to Telegram/reply `MEDIA:` drop diagnostics while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 owns configurable host roots, or should this issue also define the root-expansion contract?
rationale: The diagnostics part is a normal UX bug, but accepting more absolute host paths changes a file-read/upload security boundary and overlaps an open product direction item.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
options.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional safe user notices, while root expansion stays in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or a maintainer-approved `tools.fs.roots` design.

options.title: Use This Issue For Root Policy
options.body: Make this issue the canonical contract for configurable Telegram reply media roots, requiring schema, docs, runtime, and security tests together.

options.title: Document Current Boundary Only
options.body: Close or narrow the request after documenting that blocked absolute paths are expected unless staged under managed roots or allowed by the agent file-read policy.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots In Canonical Policy
recommendation.body: Keep this issue focused on warn-level reason logging and optional safe user notices, while root expansion stays in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/47002 or a maintainer-approved `tools.fs.roots` design.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent source-history connection to outbound media access and host-read policy.
